items.text: rings show where you are: inside a ring reached through a dot, a short column of dots at the foot of the middle, one per ring on the way, yours lit; tap one (or drag along them) to go straight there
in the Material ring, each color part's first dot wears its color: drag it through the scene's colors, or hold it for the color picker
the Material ring's adjust ring is named for the material (Water), not "Adjust · Water"
the Field panel's presets are whole pills again on an iPad (they were cut top and bottom); they wrap instead of scrolling

the Material ring (in the rings' switch): pick the water's surface (still, drip, rain, wake, glass) and, below, adjust it: its looks, its colors part by part, what makes its ripples; its middle switches the surface on and off; every material is defined once, so new ones join the ring by themselves
Settings › Pro key has a paste button: copy a key anywhere, tap paste, and it goes in (an installed app does not see a key opened as a link in the browser)
the studio's own key says Studio in Settings, with the tiers it opens
Light, watercolor, pattern walls, rain filling the pool (with its drains) and sequences go back into the studio while they are finished

what fills the pool are now three switches that combine (over bars, with sound, your finger: any of them at once); changing them never changes how much water there is, the filling just goes on from the water there is; turning them all off lets the pool finish filling over two bars instead of jumping full
with sound, the pool keeps filling as long as there is sound, faster when louder
watercolor: an ink drop brings its own water, so it spreads where it lands even on a floor still filling; ink starts falling from an eighth full
watercolor rings and swirls stay sharp instead of slowly melting; a finger combs the ink more strongly
Settings › Problems › self-test report: checks every part now and shows the last report kept on this device, so a report closed too soon can still be sent
where copying is refused (inside another app, as a preview in Claude), the report shows in the card itself, selected, ready to copy

watercolor (Pro; Water › Surface › watercolor): drops of colored ink fall into the clear water as it fills, from a third full, and swirl in it (swirl), or ink and clear water fall in turn at one spot and the ink spreads in rings, as on a suminagashi bath (rings); a tap drops your own; the ink stays where the water dries; clear ink, or dry again, gives clear water
